newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on spillover from corn, soy.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on spillover from corn, soy.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended broadly higher on spillover from gains in CBOT corn and soybeans, traders said.
KCBT wheat posted double-digit gains early in sympathy with corn and soybeans, which soared on concern over possible damage from hot, dry weather over the weekend in the U.S. Midwest.
"Wheat's fortunes were tied to corn and beans today," a KCBT trader said.
Traders said funds covered short positions early as buy stops were hit.
"Once we got all the short covering done, we quieted down quite a bit," the KCBT trader said.
Traders said wheat also drew support from news an Egyptian mill bought 55,000 tonnes of U.S. HRW wheat.
KCBT wheat settled six to 13 cents per bushel higher, with July up 13 cents at $3.44. September gained eight cents to close at $3.44.

Traders said ADM's commodity brokerage Benson-Quinn bought eight million Sept bushels. E. D. & F. Man International bought 4.6 million Sept and 1.2 million March but sold 1.7 million Sept. Rosenthal Collins sold 4.5 million Sept.
